questions.question: State Bessel’s inequality and explain. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html: • Question:- State Bessel’s inequality and explain. Answer:- Let {e1,e2,..., eM,..., eN} form an orthonormal basis in N- dimensional vector space(inner product space) H. Then for any vector x ∈ H, MX i=1 |〈x|ei〉|2 ≤ ∥x∥2. Where the equality holds if M = N. If M < N Then inequality results. 2 mark x = PNi=1〈x|ei〉ei and ∥x∥2 = NX i=1 |〈x|ei〉|2 Let xM = PMi=1〈x|ei〉ei and ∥xM∥2 = MX i=1 |〈x|ei〉|2 xM be the projection of the vector x onto a subspace spanned by the basis set {e1,e2,..., eM}, which is a subset of {e1,e2,..., eM,... eN}. Then,∥x∥2 = ∥xM∥2 + ∥x − xM∥2(Pythagorean theorem). Or any other Correct/Sensible Answer/Explanation - 1 mark

questions.question: Define orthonormality of base vectors. Why is it important in vector spaces? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Question:- Define orthonormality of base vectors. Why is it important in vector spaces? Answer:- Let {e1,e2,e3,..., en} be a set of basis vectors in a vector space(an inner product space)H. These vectors form an orthonormal basis 〈ei|e j〉 = δi j, where δi j =    1, if i = j, 0, if i ̸= j. OR
  • • Orthogonality: 〈ei|e j〉 = 0 for all i ̸= j, meaning that the projection of one vector onto the other is zero, and therefore the vectors are linearly independent.
  • • Normalization: 〈ei|ei〉 = 1 for all i, meaning that each vector has a unit length. Or any other Correct/Sensible Answer - 2 mark i. The orthonormality condition ensures that any vector a ∈ H can be expressed uniquely as a = nX i=1 〈a|ei〉ei where the coefficients 〈a,ei〉 represent the components of a along the respective directions of the basis vectors. ii. Using the orthonormality condition inner products and norms can be simplified to 〈a|b〉 = nX i=1 aibi and ∥a∥2 = nX i=1 |ai|2 where ai = 〈a|ei〉 and bi = 〈b|ei〉. Hence, orthonormal bases greatly simplify vector decomposition, projections, and its computations. Any one or any other Correct/Sensible Answer -1 mark

questions.question: Define an upper triangular matrix and give any one property of it . / [CO2]
questions.solution_html: • Question:- Define an upper triangular matrix and give any one property of it. Answer:- An upper triangular matrix is a square matrix in which all the elements below the principal diagonal(main diagonal) are zero. OR Mathematically, for an n × n matrix A = [ai j], ai j = 0 for all i > j Or any other Correct/Sensible Answer - 2 mark OR Example:- Any accurate example of an upper triangular matrix - 112 markProperties: I. The determinant of an upper triangular matrix is equal to the product of its principal diagonal (main diagonal) elements. det(A) = a11 × a22 × · · · ×ann II. For an upper triangular matrix, the eigenvalues are exactly the entries on its principal diagonal(main diagonal). III. The inverse of a non-singular upper triangular matrix is also an upper triangular matrix. Any one Or any other Correct/Sensible Answer - 1 mark

questions.question: Show that / [CO1, CO7]
questions.solution_html: • Question:- Show that [a,b,c] = [b,c,a] Answer:- The scalar triple product of three vectors is defined as [a,b,c] = a ·(b ×c) and can be written in determinant form as [a,b,c] = ﬂﬂﬂﬂﬂﬂﬂﬂax a y azbx b y bzcx c y cz ﬂﬂﬂﬂﬂﬂﬂﬂ = ﬂﬂﬂﬂﬂﬂﬂﬂbx b y bzcx c y czax a y azﬂﬂﬂﬂﬂﬂﬂﬂ This determinant represents the volume of the parallelepiped formed by the vectors a,b and c. Hence, [a,b,c] = [b,c,a] = [c,a,b]. Therefore the scalar triple product is invariant under cyclic permutation. OR The scalar triple product ([a,b,c]) can be written as the determinant of a (3×3) matrix whose rows (or columns) are the components of the three vectors (a,b, and c). Now, if we move the first row to the last and shift the others up that is, perform a cyclic change of rows-the value of a determinant does not change. Therefore, when we cyclically rearrange the vectors as ([b,c,a]), the value of the determinant remains the same. Hence, [a,b,c] = [b,c,a] because cyclic permutations of rows (or vectors) do not affect the determinant’s value. Or any other Correct/Sensible Answer - 5 mark
